title: How to use this repo (coding agents)
summary: This is an enterprise-augmented fork of Donne Martin's System Design Primer. The original study guide is unchanged under [Original study guide](README.md#original-study-guide) in [README.md](README.md). Solutions and translations are untouched. New material is for designing and building production systems.

title: Contributing
summary: Pull requests are welcome. GitHub Issues are intentionally turned off, so open a pull request instead of requesting a change. AI-assisted pull requests are welcome.

title: Enterprise guide
summary: Production topics the System Design Primer does not cover, split into short decision-oriented pages.

title: Contract testing
summary: Check producer and consumer agreements in CI so a shared staging environment is not the only integration test.

title: API gateways
summary: Put edge concerns at the gateway and keep product policy in the service that owns the data.

title: Rate limiting
summary: Choose a limiter algorithm from whether bursts are allowed, and key it on the identity that should pay the cost.

title: REST, gRPC, and GraphQL
summary: Pick one style per boundary from who the caller is, whether the shape is stable, and who pays for round trips.

title: API versioning
summary: Evolve contracts compatibly, and introduce an explicit version only when a break is unavoidable.

title: Webhooks
summary: Sign each delivery, retry with backoff, and make the receiver dedupe on an event id.

title: Tamper-evident audit logs
summary: Record privileged actions in an append-only log that operators cannot quietly edit, and keep it separate from debug logs.

title: HIPAA and PCI DSS basics
summary: Shrink the systems that touch PHI or cardholder data, and put the extra controls only on what remains.

title: GDPR and CCPA basics
summary: Inventory personal data, minimize it, and build export and deletion as product paths rather than as tickets.

title: Data residency
summary: Pin a tenant's data, backups, and operator access to the regions the contract allows.

title: Retention and deletion
summary: Give every store a retention period and a deletion path that includes indexes, vendors, and backups.

title: SOC 2 basics
summary: Treat SOC 2 as an attestation that named controls operated over a period, and build the evidence those controls need.

title: Cost allocation
summary: Attribute shared spend to teams and tenants with tags and a written split, so showback is explainable.

title: Capacity planning
summary: Turn the traffic estimate into a resource plan with headroom, a lead time, and a date to revisit.

title: FinOps
summary: Make spend visible to the teams who cause it, and review it on a cadence with the same seriousness as an SLO.

title: Unit economics
summary: Express cost per business unit so a design change can be compared to the revenue or the budget it serves.

title: Change data capture
summary: Stream committed database changes from the log when consumers need the row-level history the database already committed.

title: Event-driven architecture
summary: Publish facts that already happened, let consumers build their own state, and treat delivery as at-least-once.

title: Data governance
summary: Assign an owner, a classification, a lineage, and an access rule to data people will rely on.

title: Idempotency
summary: Make a retried request return the original result, and reject the same key when the body differs.

title: Sagas
summary: Split a multi-service business transaction into local steps plus compensations, and choose a choreography or an orchestrator.

title: Schema evolution
summary: Change events and tables so old and new producers and consumers overlap for at least one release.

title: Transactional outbox
summary: Write the business change and the message you must publish in the same database transaction, then publish asynchronously.

title: Warehouse and lakehouse
summary: Keep operational stores for transactions, and land analytical copies in a warehouse or a table format on object storage.

title: CI and CD
summary: Build an artifact once, test it, sign it, and promote that same digest through environments.

title: Database migrations and rollback
summary: Change schemas in expand and contract steps so the previous application version still runs, and so rollback does not require time travel.

title: Feature flags
summary: Separate release from deploy with short-lived flags, and make the off state safe when the flag service is down.

title: Infrastructure as code and environments
summary: Describe infrastructure in reviewed code, and keep environments separated without copying production personal data downhill.

title: Progressive delivery
summary: Expose a release to a small slice first, watch the SLO, and expand or roll back on that evidence.

title: Authorization models
summary: Choose RBAC, ABAC, or ReBAC for the decision, and enforce it on the server from the authenticated identity.

title: OIDC and OAuth 2.0
summary: Pick an OAuth 2.0 flow, bind tokens to the right audience, and treat OpenID Connect as the identity layer on top.

title: SSO and SAML
summary: Accept enterprise single sign-on through SAML 2.0 when a customer IdP requires it, and keep the assertion checks strict.

title: Secrets management
summary: Keep secrets in a manager, inject them at runtime, scope who can read them, and rotate them without a redeploy heroics story.

title: Service-to-service auth
summary: Give every workload an identity and a short-lived credential, using workload identity, SPIFFE, or mutually authenticated TLS.

title: Anti-corruption layer
summary: Translate between a legacy model and a new model in one place, so the new model does not grow the legacy system's concepts.

title: Modular monolith
summary: Keep one deployable, split it into modules with hard boundaries, and extract a service only when a team or a scale number requires it.

title: Strangler fig
summary: Put a seam in front of the legacy system and replace one capability at a time until the old path can be deleted.

title: Alerting and on-call
summary: Page a named owner on user-visible symptoms that threaten the error budget, and keep a human rotation that can act.

title: Incident response
summary: Declare early, assign roles, mitigate first, and keep a timeline that the postmortem can trust.

title: OpenTelemetry
summary: Instrument with OpenTelemetry and put sampling, redaction, and vendor export in the collector, not in application code.

title: Blameless postmortems
summary: Write what happened, why the system allowed it, and which actions will change the system, without blaming a person.

title: SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets
summary: Define a user-visible indicator, set a target over a window, and spend the error budget on purpose.

title: Logs, metrics, and traces
summary: Use metrics for symptoms and alerts, traces for one request's path, and logs for the detail you cannot aggregate.

title: Conway's law
summary: Expect the system to mirror team communication, and change the team boundary when you want a different system boundary.

title: ADRs and RFCs
summary: Use an RFC to shape a proposal with the people it affects, and an ADR to record the decision you actually made.

title: Service ownership
summary: Give every service and store one owning team that ships it, runs it, and answers for its data.

title: Platform teams
summary: Run an internal platform as a product with customers, a golden path, and a support model that is not a ticket black hole.

title: Team topologies
summary: Organize teams by the kind of work they do and the way they are allowed to interact, so delivery is not an accident of the org chart.

title: Reference architectures
summary: Four end-to-end designs with requirements, estimates, a diagram, tradeoffs, and a severity-ranked design review.

title: Reference architecture: data platform
summary: CDC from operational databases into a lakehouse with owned curated tables, deletion, and a catalog.

title: Reference architecture: event-driven orders and payments
summary: Checkout as an orchestrated saga with an outbox, idempotent charges, and inventory reservation.

title: Reference architecture: internal platform with SSO and audit
summary: An internal developer platform with corporate SSO, a service catalog, and a tamper-evident audit log.

title: Reference architecture: multi-tenant B2B SaaS
summary: A pooled work-management SaaS with a bridge tier for large tenants, SSO, and tenant-scoped webhooks.

title: Chaos testing
summary: Run a small, reversible fault with a hypothesis and an abort switch, and write down what broke.

title: Circuit breakers and bulkheads
summary: Stop calling a dependency that is failing, and isolate its concurrency so it cannot sink the whole process.

title: Disaster recovery, RPO, and RTO
summary: Name how much data you can lose and how fast you must be back, then test the restore that those numbers require.

title: Load shedding
summary: Reject excess work early, with a clear retry signal, before the process collapses under queueing delay.

title: Multi-region architectures
summary: Choose active-passive or active-active from the RPO, the RTO, and whether two regions may write the same key.

title: Retries, backoff, and timeouts
summary: Bound every remote call with a timeout, and retry only idempotent work with jittered backoff.

title: Encryption and key management
summary: Encrypt in transit and at rest with managed keys, separate data keys from key-encryption keys, and do not invent a cipher.

title: OWASP ASVS chapter map
summary: Point a design at the ASVS 5.0.0 chapter that covers the control, without copying the standard's requirement text.

title: Software supply chain
summary: Know what you build, produce an SBOM, sign the artifact, and deploy only what you verified.

title: Threat modeling with STRIDE
summary: Walk the data flows once per trust boundary and name spoofing, tampering, repudiation, disclosure, denial of service, and elevation of privilege.

title: Zero trust
summary: Authenticate and authorize every request, and treat network location as an untrusted hint.

title: Per-tenant data and keys
summary: Put the tenant on every record and decide which tenants get their own encryption key.

title: Tenant isolation models
summary: Pick silo, pool, or bridge isolation per tier of tenant, and write down what a bug in one model can leak.

title: Tenant onboarding and offboarding
summary: Provision a tenant as a record plus policy, and offboard it including access, exports, deletion, and backups.

title: Noisy neighbors
summary: Cap one tenant's load so a shared pool stays fair, and move a tenant to a silo when caps are not enough.

title: Tenant-aware routing
summary: Resolve the tenant from the credential and the host, then send the request to that tenant's home region or cell.

title: What's dated in the Primer
summary: Where the System Design Primer's advice shows its era, and the current equivalent to use in a design.

title: adr-writer
summary: Use this when recording an architecture decision: context, the decision, alternatives rejected and why, consequences, and status, as an Architecture Decision Record.

title: ADR-NNNN: Title in the imperative
summary: - Status: Proposed - Date: YYYY-MM-DD - Owners: team that lives with the decision

title: design-reviewer
summary: Use this when reviewing a proposed software architecture or system design for production gaps: single points of failure, cache invalidation, consistency, 10x load, failure modes, authentication and authorization, OWASP ASVS, compliance, observability, retention, cost, migration, and team boundaries.

title: Design review checklist
summary: Walk in order. Each item is a question about the design in front of you. The severity scale and the output shape live in [SKILL.md](SKILL.md). Primer patterns for caches, replication, and failover live in [the architect references](../system-architect/reference/scalability.md) and as cards under [patterns/](../../../patterns/README.md). ASVS chapter titles below are identifiers from the OWASP ASVS

title: system-architect
summary: Use this when turning a feature or product request into an enterprise system design: functional and non-functional requirements, back-of-the-envelope traffic, storage, and bandwidth estimates, a mermaid component sketch, a data model, an API outline, and explicit tradeoffs.

title: Pattern cards
summary: One card per pattern with the problem, when to use it, when not to, tradeoffs, and failure modes.

title: Anti-corruption layer
summary: Translate between a new model and a legacy or external model so foreign concepts stay at the edge.

title: API gateway
summary: A single edge that authenticates, limits, and routes requests, without owning product decisions.

title: Availability and failover
summary: Stand up a second copy and a tested promotion path so one failure does not end the service.

title: Backend for frontend
summary: A server-side API shaped for one client, aggregating downstream services so the client does not.

title: Blue/green
summary: Run two complete environments and switch traffic from the live color to the idle one.

title: Bulkhead
summary: Give each dependency or tenant a separate concurrency limit so one failure cannot take every thread.

title: Cache-aside
summary: The application reads the cache, and on a miss loads the store and fills the cache.

title: Cache invalidation
summary: Define who may overwrite or delete a cached entry and the maximum staleness a caller can observe.

title: Canary
summary: Send a small fraction of traffic to the new version and expand only if the user-visible metrics hold.

title: Change data capture
summary: Read committed row changes from the database log and stream them to other systems.

title: Content delivery network
summary: Serve cacheable bytes from a location near the user so the origin does not see that request.

title: Circuit breaker
summary: Stop calling a dependency that is failing, fail fast for a cool-down, then try a few probes.

title: Consistency patterns
summary: Choose weak, eventual, or strong consistency per path, and write the partition behavior separately from the healthy-path latency.

title: CQRS
summary: Use a write model shaped for commands and a read model shaped for queries, updated asynchronously.

title: Denormalization
summary: Store a copy of a field next to the data that reads it, so a hot path does not join.

title: Event sourcing
summary: Store the state of an aggregate as an append-only sequence of domain events and derive current state by fold.

title: Feature flags
summary: Branch behavior at runtime so you can ship code dark, open it gradually, or turn it off without a redeploy.

title: Federation
summary: Split databases by function so each domain has its own store and its own write path.

title: Idempotency keys
summary: Store the result of a write under a client-supplied key so a retry returns the same result and does not repeat the effect.

title: Load balancing
summary: Spread requests across healthy targets so one instance is not the user-facing capacity or the single failure.

title: Load shedding
summary: Reject new work when the service is past a defined saturation point so accepted work can finish.

title: Message queues and async processing
summary: Accept work onto a durable queue and let a worker finish it after the user request returns.

title: Rate limiting
summary: Count or meter requests per identity and reject the excess before the service is overloaded.

title: Refresh-ahead
summary: The cache reloads a hot entry before its TTL expires so the next reader does not pay for a miss.

title: Leader-follower replication
summary: One leader accepts writes and replicates them to followers that serve reads.

title: Multi-leader replication
summary: More than one node accepts writes, and the nodes converge, with conflicts when they write the same key.

title: Retry with backoff
summary: Repeat a failed idempotent call with exponential delay and jitter, and stop at a budget.

title: Reverse proxy
summary: A proxy in front of the origin terminates client connections and can cache, compress, and hide the origin.

title: Saga
summary: Complete a business transaction as a series of local commits with explicit compensations.

title: Sharding
summary: Split one dataset so each node holds a subset of the keys, usually by hash or by range.

title: Sidecar and service mesh
summary: Run a helper process beside each instance to do mTLS, retries, and telemetry, or adopt a mesh when many services need those uniformly.

title: Strangler fig
summary: Route capabilities one at a time from a legacy system to a new one behind a stable facade, then delete the old path.

title: Transactional outbox
summary: Commit the business write and the outbound message in one database transaction, then publish asynchronously.

title: Write-behind
summary: The application writes the cache and the store is updated asynchronously after the caller has been told success.

title: Write-through
summary: The application writes the cache and the cache writes the store before the write returns.

title: Templates
summary: Copyable templates for a design doc, an ADR, a threat model, an SLO, a runbook, a postmortem, and a capacity worksheet.

title: ADR template pointer
summary: The canonical Architecture Decision Record template lives with the adr-writer skill. Copy that file, not a second variant.

title: Capacity estimate worksheet
summary: A worksheet for request rate, bandwidth, storage, the first bottleneck, and the cost driver.

title: Design doc template
summary: Outline for a system design with requirements, estimates, a component sketch, data, API, and tradeoffs.

title: Postmortem template
summary: A blameless incident write-up with a timeline, impact, contributing factors, and owned actions.

title: Runbook template
summary: The steps on-call follows for one page, including how to tell that the mitigation worked.

title: SLO template
summary: A one-page definition of an SLI, its target and window, and what happens when the error budget burns.

title: Threat model template
summary: A STRIDE worksheet tied to the trust boundaries of one design.
